/-! ## Project-local Mathlib supplement — annihilator ideal sheaf and schematic support

These declarations build the annihilator ideal sheaf of a sheaf of modules and the
support/properness predicates of `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`,
§"Support and freeness predicates". Mathlib (at the pinned commit) carries no
annihilator ideal sheaf for sheaves of modules on a scheme, nor a schematic-support
or proper-support predicate, so they are built here.

The annihilator is packaged via `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, exactly mirroring
Mathlib's `Scheme.Hom.ker` (which is `ofIdeals fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom`):
`ofIdeals` produces *the largest ideal sheaf contained in* an arbitrary affine-local
family of ideals, so the structure's `map_ideal_basicOpen` coherence is discharged
internally and need not be supplied at definition time. The basic-open coherence that
makes the local annihilators agree with `ofIdeals` (the analogue of `Hom.ker_apply`,
`def:modules_annihilator`) is the separate characterization lemma `annihilator_ideal`,
which depends on the not-yet-closed QCoh→localization bridge
`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen` (`lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`) together with
the algebra engine `Module.annihilator_isLocalizedModule_eq_map`
(`lem:annihilator_localization_eq_map`); see the handoff in
`task_results/.../QuotScheme.md`. -/

namespace Scheme.Modules

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- The **annihilator ideal sheaf** of a sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X`
(`def:modules_annihilator`).

On each affine open `U`, the intended section is the annihilator
`Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` of the `Γ(X,U)`-module of sections `Γ(F,U)`. The ideal sheaf
is assembled with `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, the largest ideal sheaf contained
in that affine-local family — exactly the construction used for `Scheme.Hom.ker`. This
sidesteps proving the basic-open coherence (`map_ideal_basicOpen`) at definition time;
the identity `(annihilator F).ideal U = Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` is the downstream
characterization lemma (`annihilator_ideal`, blocked on the QCoh localization bridge).

This is a project-local primitive: Mathlib does not carry an annihilator ideal sheaf
for sheaves of modules on a scheme. -/
noncomputable def annihilator (F : X.Modules) : X.IdealSheafData :=
  IdealSheafData.ofIdeals fun U => Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)

/-- The component of the annihilator ideal sheaf at an affine open is contained in the
module annihilator of the sections. This is the always-available (`ofIdeals`) direction
of the characterization; the reverse inclusion is the basic-open coherence blocked on
`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/
lemma annihilator_ideal_le (F : X.Modules) (U : X.affineOpens) :
    (annihilator F).ideal U ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1) :=
  IdealSheafData.ideal_ofIdeals_le _ _

/-- The **schematic support** of a sheaf of modules `F` on a scheme `X`
(`def:schematic_support`): the closed subscheme of `X` cut out by the annihilator
ideal sheaf `annihilator F`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/
noncomputable def schematicSupport (F : X.Modules) : Scheme.{u} :=
  (annihilator F).subscheme

/-- The canonical closed immersion of the schematic support into the ambient scheme,
realizing `schematicSupport F` as a closed subscheme of `X` (`def:schematic_support`).
This is the `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` of the annihilator ideal sheaf; it is a
`IsPreimmersion` + `QuasiCompact` immersion onto the support. Project-local because
`annihilator` is. -/
noncomputable def schematicSupportι (F : X.Modules) : schematicSupport F ⟶ X :=
  (annihilator F).subschemeι

/-- The sheaf of modules `F` **has proper support over `S` along `f`**
(`def:has_proper_support`): the composite of the schematic-support immersion with
`f : X ⟶ S` is a proper morphism. Since `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper` is stable under
base change, this condition is preserved by pullback, as required by the Quot functor's
pullback action. Project-local because `schematicSupport` is. -/
def HasProperSupport {S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (F : X.Modules) : Prop :=
  IsProper (schematicSupportι F ≫ f)

end Scheme.Modules

end AlgebraicGeometry

4064	\begin{lemma}[Tilde--global-sections adjunction on an affine scheme]
4065	  \label{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib}
4066	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.adjunction}
4067	  \mathlibok
4068	  \textit{Provided by Mathlib (\texttt{Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Tilde}).}
4069	  For a commutative ring \(R\), the tilde functor
4070	  \(\widetilde{(\cdot)} : \mathrm{Mod}_{R} \to (\Spec R).\mathrm{Modules}\)
4071	  is left adjoint to the global-sections functor
4072	  \(\Gamma(\Spec R, -) : (\Spec R).\mathrm{Modules} \to \mathrm{Mod}_{R}\)
4073	  (\texttt{moduleSpecΓFunctor}); the unit is the isomorphism
4074	  \(M \to \Gamma(\widetilde M, \top)\) and the counit is the
4075	  tilde--\(\Gamma\) comparison
4076	  \(\widetilde{\Gamma(\mathcal N, \top)} \to \mathcal N\)
4077	  (\texttt{fromTildeΓ}). Mathlib also supplies the two companion
4078	  adjunctions used with it below: extension--restriction of scalars
4079	  \(B \otimes_A - \dashv \mathrm{res}_\varphi\)
4080	  (\texttt{ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj}) and
4081	  pullback--pushforward \(\pi^* \dashv \pi_*\) for sheaves of modules
4082	  over schemes (\texttt{Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction}).
4083	\end{lemma}

4085	\begin{lemma}[Global sections of the pushforward as restricted scalars]
4086	  \label{lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge}
4087	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackTilde_gammaBridge}
4088	  \leanok
4089	  \uses{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib, lem:modules_pullback_mathlib}
4090	  For a ring homomorphism \(\varphi : A \to B\) with
4091	  \(\pi = \Spec\varphi : \Spec B \to \Spec A\), the two functors
4092	  \((\Spec B).\mathrm{Modules} \to \mathrm{Mod}_{A}\)
4093	  \[
4094	    \mathcal N \longmapsto \Gamma(\Spec A,\, \pi_{*}\mathcal N)
4095	    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
4096	    \mathcal N \longmapsto \mathrm{res}_{\varphi}\, \Gamma(\Spec B,\, \mathcal N)
4097	  \]
4098	  (global sections of the pushforward, with \(A\) acting through
4099	  \(\Gamma(\pi^{\sharp})\); respectively global sections, with \(A\)
4100	  acting through \(\varphi\)) are naturally isomorphic.
4101	\end{lemma}
4102	\begin{proof}
4103	  \leanok
4104	  \uses{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib, lem:modules_pullback_mathlib}
4105	  On carriers the component at \(\mathcal N\) is restriction of sections
4106	  along the equality of opens \(\pi^{-1}(\Spec A) = \Spec B\), a
4107	  bijection. It is \(A\)-linear: for \(a \in A\) the action on the
4108	  source is by \(\Gamma(\pi^{\sharp})(\iota_A(a))\) and on the target by
4109	  \(\iota_B(\varphi(a))\), where
4110	  \(\iota_R : R \cong \Gamma(\Spec R, \mathcal O)\) is the canonical
4111	  identification; these agree by naturality of \(\iota\) in \(R\)
4112	  applied to \(\varphi\) (that is,
4113	  \(\Gamma(\pi^{\sharp}) \circ \iota_A = \iota_B \circ \varphi\)),
4114	  combined with semilinearity of section restriction for the module
4115	  sheaf \(\mathcal N\). Naturality in \(\mathcal N\) is naturality of
4116	  section restriction against module-sheaf morphisms.
4117	\end{proof}

4120	  \label{lem:pullback_tildeIso}

4122	  \leanok
4123	  \uses{def:quot_pullback_app_isoTensor}
4124	  \textit{Source: Stacks~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01HQ}{01HQ}
4125	  / \href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BJ8}{0BJ8} (pullback of
4126	  quasi-coherent modules along a Spec morphism).}
4127	  For a ring homomorphism \(\varphi : A \to B\) and an \(A\)-module
4128	  \(M\), there is a canonical iso between the pullback of the
4129	  tilde-sheaf and the tilde of the base-changed module:
4130	  \[
4131	    (\mathtt{Scheme.Modules.pullback}\, (\mathrm{Spec.map}\, \varphi)).\mathrm{obj}\,
4132	      (\widetilde{M})
4133	    \;\cong\;
4134	    \widetilde{B \otimes_A M}.
4135	  \]
4136	  Mathlib \texttt{b80f227} ships
4137	  \texttt{PullbackFree.lean:122 pullbackObjFreeIso} for \emph{free} sheaves
4138	  only — the general-module form (Stacks 01HQ) is unowned.
4139	\end{lemma}

4141	  \leanok
4142	  \uses{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib, lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge,
4143	    def:quot_pullback_app_isoTensor}
4144	  Write \(\pi = \Spec\varphi : \Spec B \to \Spec A\). Both composite
4145	  functors
4146	  \[
4147	    \mathrm{Mod}_{A} \xrightarrow{\ \widetilde{(\cdot)}\ }
4148	      (\Spec A).\mathrm{Modules} \xrightarrow{\ \pi^{*}\ }
4149	      (\Spec B).\mathrm{Modules}
4150	    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
4151	    \mathrm{Mod}_{A} \xrightarrow{\ B \otimes_A -\ } \mathrm{Mod}_{B}
4152	      \xrightarrow{\ \widetilde{(\cdot)}\ } (\Spec B).\mathrm{Modules}
4153	  \]
4154	  are left adjoints: the first of
4155	  \(\mathcal N \mapsto \Gamma(\Spec A, \pi_{*}\mathcal N)\) (compose the
4156	  tilde--\(\Gamma\) adjunction on \(\Spec A\),
4157	  \cref{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib}, with
4158	  \(\pi^{*} \dashv \pi_{*}\)), the second of
4159	  \(\mathcal N \mapsto \mathrm{res}_{\varphi}\,\Gamma(\Spec B, \mathcal N)\)
4160	  (compose extension--restriction of scalars along \(\varphi\) with the
4161	  tilde--\(\Gamma\) adjunction on \(\Spec B\)). By
4162	  \cref{lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge} the two right adjoints are
4163	  naturally isomorphic, so uniqueness of left adjoints yields a natural
4164	  isomorphism of the two composites; its component at \(M\) is the
4165	  required isomorphism
4166	  \(\pi^{*}\widetilde M \cong \widetilde{B \otimes_A M}\).
4167	
4168	  For the section-level identity, apply the unit compatibility of the
4169	  left-adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism at \(m \in M\): the unit of the
4170	  first composed adjunction sends \(m\) to the canonical base map
4171	  (\cref{def:quot_pullback_app_isoTensor}, at \(V = U = \top\)) of the
4172	  global section of \(\widetilde M\) attached to \(m\), while the unit
4173	  of the second sends \(m\) to the global section of
4174	  \(\widetilde{B \otimes_A M}\) attached to \(1 \otimes m\); the
4175	  compatibility square states precisely that the isomorphism carries
4176	  the former to the latter.
4177	\end{proof}

4396	  pullback of \(\mathcal N\) along \texttt{hV.fromSpec} is canonically
4397	  isomorphic to \texttt{tilde} of its sections:

4403	    \quad\text{(on \(\mathrm{Spec}\,\Gamma(X, V)\)).}
4404	  \]

4407	  partial), but the general statement

4415	    lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib}
4416	  Write \(j = \mathtt{hV.fromSpec} : \Spec\Gamma(X,V) \to X\) (an open
4417	  immersion with image \(V\)) and \(G = j^{*}\mathcal N\). Pullback along an
4418	  open immersion preserves quasi-coherence
4419	  (Lean \texttt{isQuasicoherent\_pullback\_fromSpec}), so \(G\) is a
4420	  quasi-coherent module on the affine scheme \(\Spec\Gamma(X,V)\); by the
4421	  affine structure theorem (Stacks 01I8, Lean
4422	  \texttt{isIso\_fromTildeΓ\_of\_isQuasicoherent}) the tilde--\(\Gamma\)
4423	  counit \(\widetilde{\Gamma(G,\top)} \to G\) is an isomorphism.
4424	
4425	  The canonical base map \(b : \Gamma(\mathcal N, V) \to \Gamma(G, \top)\)
4426	  (the \(V\)-sections of the pullback--pushforward adjunction unit followed by
4427	  restriction along \(\top \le j^{-1}V\)) is bijective. Indeed the two
4428	  adjunctions \(\mathrm{restrict} \dashv j_{*}\) and \(j^{*} \dashv j_{*}\)
4429	  share the right adjoint, so their units are identified through the canonical
4430	  natural isomorphism \(\mathrm{restrict} \cong j^{*}\)
4431	  (\cref{lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib}). Under this
4432	  identification, the \(V\)-component of the unit of the restriction
4433	  adjunction is the presheaf restriction of \(\mathcal N\) along the
4434	  \emph{equality} of opens \(j(j^{-1}V) = V\), hence bijective; the component
4435	  of the natural isomorphism is bijective; and the final restriction is along
4436	  the equality \(\top = j^{-1}V\). Thus \(b\) is a composite of three
4437	  bijections.

4439	  Since \(b\) is a bijective \(\Gamma(X,V)\)-linear map (the
4440	  \(\Gamma(X,V)\)-action on \(\Gamma(G,\top)\) being through the canonical
4441	  ring isomorphism \(\Gamma(X,V) \cong \Gamma(\Spec\Gamma(X,V),\top)\)),
4442	  it induces an isomorphism
4443	  \(\widetilde{b} : \widetilde{\Gamma(\mathcal N,V)} \cong
4444	  \widetilde{\Gamma(G,\top)}\). The required isomorphism is the inverse of
4445	  \(\widetilde{b}\) followed by the counit. The characterizing section
4446	  identity holds because \(\widetilde{(-)}\)-functoriality intertwines the
4447	  canonical maps \(M \to \Gamma(\widetilde M, U)\) (naturality of
4448	  \texttt{toOpen}), while the counit composed with \(\mathtt{toOpen}\) at
4449	  \(\top\) is the identity restriction.

/-! ### The dévissage frame for full algebraic generic freeness

Grothendieck's generic-freeness lemma (blueprint
`thm:generic_flatness_algebraic`, Nitsure §4 "Lemma on Generic Flatness"):
for `A` a noetherian domain, `B` a finite-type `A`-algebra and `M` a finite
`B`-module there is `f ≠ 0` in `A` with `M_f` free over `A_f`.

Nitsure's proof has two layers: a *dévissage* (prime filtration of `M` as a
module over the noetherian ring `B`, reducing to `M = B/𝔭`, via the splicing
fact that generic freeness is stable under extensions), and a *domain core*
(`M = B/𝔭`: Noether normalisation over `Frac A` + clearing denominators +
the generic-rank exact sequence + induction on fibre dimension). This
section proves the dévissage layer completely — the splicing lemma
`genericallyFree_of_exact` (via `ModuleCat.free_shortExact` and the
localization-transport lemma `free_localizedModule_powers_mul`), the torsion
base case `genericallyFree_of_torsion` (Nitsure's `n = -1`), and the
assembly `genericFlatnessAlgebraic` via
`IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime` — leaving the
domain core `genericallyFree_quotient_prime` as the single typed `sorry`. -/

/-- The **generic-freeness property** of an `A`-module `M`: some localization
`M_f` at a single non-zero `f ∈ A` is a free module over `A_f`. This is the
conclusion shared by every statement of this section. -/
def GenericallyFree (A : Type*) (M : Type*) [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module A M] : Prop :=
  ∃ f : A, f ≠ 0 ∧
    Module.Free (Localization.Away f) (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M)

/-- Generic freeness transports along enlarging the inverted element: if `M_f`
is free over `A_f` then `M_{fg}` is free over `A_{fg}` for every `g`. The
proof is base-change associativity
`A_{fg} ⊗_{A_f} (A_f ⊗_A M) ≅ A_{fg} ⊗_A M` together with freeness of base
change (`Module.Free.tensor`); the two tensor legs are identified with the
localized modules by `IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange`. -/
theorem free_localizedModule_powers_mul (A : Type*) (M : Type*) [CommRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] (f g : A)
    (hf : Module.Free (Localization.Away f)
      (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M)) :
    Module.Free (Localization.Away (f * g))
      (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f * g)) M) := by
  haveI := hf
  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away f) (Localization.Away (f * g)) :=
    (IsLocalization.awayToAwayRight (S := Localization.Away f)
      (P := Localization.Away (f * g)) f g).toAlgebra
  haveI : IsScalarTower A (Localization.Away f) (Localization.Away (f * g)) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun a =>
      (IsLocalization.awayToAwayRight_eq (S := Localization.Away f)
        (P := Localization.Away (f * g)) f g a).symm

    (inferInstance : Module.Free (Localization.Away (f * g))

        (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M))) ?_

      (Localization.Away (f * g))
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers (f * g)) M)).equiv)

      (Localization.Away (f * g)) (Localization.Away (f * g)) M)

    (LinearEquiv.refl (Localization.Away (f * g)) (Localization.Away (f * g)))
    ((IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange (Submonoid.powers f) (Localization.Away f)
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) M)).equiv)).symm

/-- Generic freeness is invariant under `A`-linear equivalence. -/
theorem GenericallyFree.of_linearEquiv {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {M N : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (e : M ≃ₗ[A] N) (h : GenericallyFree A M) : GenericallyFree A N := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfree⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, hf, ?_⟩
  haveI := hfree
  have e' : LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) M ≃ₗ[A]
      LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) N :=
    IsLocalizedModule.iso (Submonoid.powers f)
      ((LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Submonoid.powers f) N) ∘ₗ e.toLinearMap)
  exact Module.Free.of_equiv' hfree
    (e'.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization (Submonoid.powers f) (Localization.Away f))

/-- **Splicing lemma for generic freeness** — the extension step of Nitsure's
dévissage. If the outer terms of a short exact sequence
`0 → M₁ → M₂ → M₃ → 0` of `A`-modules are generically free, so is the middle
term: localize the sequence at the product of the two witnesses (exactness of
localization) and apply `ModuleCat.free_shortExact`. -/
theorem genericallyFree_of_exact {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    {M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*} [AddCommGroup M₁] [Module A M₁] [AddCommGroup M₂]
    [Module A M₂] [AddCommGroup M₃] [Module A M₃]
    (u : M₁ →ₗ[A] M₂) (v : M₂ →ₗ[A] M₃) (hu : Function.Injective u)
    (hv : Function.Surjective v) (huv : Function.Exact u v)
    (h₁ : GenericallyFree A M₁) (h₃ : GenericallyFree A M₃) :
    GenericallyFree A M₂ := by
  obtain ⟨f₁, hf₁, hfree₁⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨f₃, hf₃, hfree₃⟩ := h₃
  refine ⟨f₁ * f₃, mul_ne_zero hf₁ hf₃, ?_⟩
  have hfree₁' := free_localizedModule_powers_mul A M₁ f₁ f₃ hfree₁
  have hfree₃' := free_localizedModule_powers_mul A M₃ f₃ f₁ hfree₃
  rw [mul_comm f₃ f₁] at hfree₃'
  set S : Submonoid A := Submonoid.powers (f₁ * f₃) with hS
  let u₀ := IsLocalizedModule.map S (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₁)
    (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₂) u
  let v₀ := IsLocalizedModule.map S (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₂)
    (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₃) v
  have hu₀ : Function.Injective u₀ :=
    IsLocalizedModule.map_injective S (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₁)
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₂) u hu
  have hv₀ : Function.Surjective v₀ :=
    IsLocalizedModule.map_surjective S (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₂)
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₃) v hv
  have huv₀ : Function.Exact u₀ v₀ :=
    IsLocalizedModule.map_exact S (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₁)
      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₂) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M₃)
      u v huv
  let u' := u₀.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization S (Localization.Away (f₁ * f₃))
  let v' := v₀.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization S (Localization.Away (f₁ * f₃))
  let C : ShortComplex (ModuleCat (Localization.Away (f₁ * f₃))) :=
    ShortComplex.mk (ModuleCat.ofHom u') (ModuleCat.ofHom v')
      (by ext x; exact huv₀.apply_apply_eq_zero x)
  have hC : C.ShortExact :=
    { exact := C.moduleCat_exact_iff.mpr fun x hx => (huv₀ x).mp hx
      mono_f := (ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective _).mpr hu₀
      epi_g := (ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective _).mpr hv₀ }
  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.Away (f₁ * f₃)) C.X₁ := hfree₁'
  haveI : Module.Free (Localization.Away (f₁ * f₃)) C.X₃ := hfree₃'
  exact ModuleCat.free_shortExact hC

/-- Generic freeness of a subsingleton module (with `f = 1`). This is the
degenerate input to the dévissage; the substantive Nitsure base case
(`M_K = 0`, i.e. torsion `M`) is `genericallyFree_of_torsion` below. -/
theorem genericallyFree_of_subsingleton (A M : Type*) [CommRing A]
    [Nontrivial A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Subsingleton M] :
    GenericallyFree A M := by
  refine ⟨1, one_ne_zero, ?_⟩
  haveI : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (1 : A)) M) := by
    refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 fun x => ?_
    refine LocalizedModule.induction_on (fun m s => ?_) x
    rw [Subsingleton.elim m 0]
    exact LocalizedModule.zero_mk s
  infer_instance

/-- **Torsion base case** of generic freeness (Nitsure's `n = -1`, `M_K = 0`):
a finite `A`-module all of whose elements are `A`-torsion is generically free
— the product of annihilators of a finite generating set kills the module,
so the corresponding localization vanishes. -/
theorem genericallyFree_of_torsion (A M : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    (htors : ∀ m : M, ∃ a : A, a ≠ 0 ∧ a • m = 0) : GenericallyFree A M := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := (‹Module.Finite A M› : Module.Finite A M).fg_top
  choose a ha haz using htors
  refine ⟨∏ m ∈ s, a m, Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr fun m _ => ha m, ?_⟩
  have hkill : ∀ m : M, (∏ m' ∈ s, a m') • m = 0 := by
    have hker : Submodule.span A (s : Set M) ≤
        LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul A M (∏ m' ∈ s, a m')) := by
      rw [Submodule.span_le]
      intro m hm
      simp only [SetLike.mem_coe, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.lsmul_apply]
      rw [← Finset.mul_prod_erase s a hm, mul_comm, mul_smul, haz m, smul_zero]
    intro m
    have hm : m ∈ Submodule.span A (s : Set M) := by
      rw [hs]; exact Submodule.mem_top
    simpa using hker hm
  haveI : Subsingleton (LocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (∏ m ∈ s, a m)) M) := by
    refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 fun x => ?_
    refine LocalizedModule.induction_on (fun m t => ?_) x
    rw [← LocalizedModule.mk_cancel_common_left
      (⟨∏ m' ∈ s, a m', Submonoid.mem_powers _⟩ : Submonoid.powers (∏ m ∈ s, a m))
      t m]
    rw [show ((⟨∏ m' ∈ s, a m', Submonoid.mem_powers _⟩ :
        Submonoid.powers (∏ m ∈ s, a m)) : A) • m = 0 from hkill m]
    exact LocalizedModule.zero_mk _
  infer_instance

/-- **The domain core of algebraic generic freeness** [Nitsure §4, "Lemma on
Generic Flatness", normalisation step]: for a noetherian domain `A`, a
finite-type `A`-algebra `B` and a prime `𝔭 ⊆ B`, the quotient domain `B/𝔭`
is generically free over `A`.

This is the single remaining `sorry` of the dévissage: its (future) proof is
Nitsure's induction on the dimension of the generic fibre — if
`ker (A → B/𝔭) ≠ 0` the localization vanishes (`genericallyFree_of_torsion`);
otherwise Noether normalisation of `Frac A ⊗_A B/𝔭` over `Frac A`
(`exists_finite_inj_algHom_of_fg`), clearing denominators to make `(B/𝔭)_g`
module-finite over `A_g[b₁, …, b_m]` (`IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples`
+ `Polynomial.scaleRoots` integrality), the generic-rank short exact sequence
`0 → A_g[b̄]^r → (B/𝔭)_g → T → 0` with `T` torsion over the polynomial ring,
and the fibre-dimension drop feeding the outer induction. TRUE as stated
(it is a special case of Grothendieck's lemma, Stacks 051R). -/
theorem genericallyFree_quotient_prime (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    (p : Ideal B) [p.IsPrime] : GenericallyFree A (B ⧸ p) := by
  sorry

/-- **Algebraic generic freeness, dévissage assembly** [Nitsure §4 "Lemma on
Generic Flatness" / Stacks 051R; blueprint `thm:generic_flatness_algebraic`].

For a noetherian domain `A`, a finite-type `A`-algebra `B` and a finite
`B`-module `M` (with compatible `A`-structure), `M` is generically free over
`A`. The prime-filtration dévissage over the noetherian ring `B`
(`IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime`) is complete:
the subsingleton case is `genericallyFree_of_subsingleton`, prime quotients
are the domain core `genericallyFree_quotient_prime` (the one remaining
`sorry` of this section), and stability under extensions is the splicing
lemma `genericallyFree_of_exact`. -/
theorem genericFlatnessAlgebraic (A B M : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module.Finite B M] [Module A M]
    [IsScalarTower A B M] : GenericallyFree A M := by
  haveI : IsNoetherianRing B := Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing A B
  refine IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime (A := B)
    ‹Module.Finite B M›
    (motive := fun N iACG iMB _ => ∀ (iA : Module A N),
      (@IsScalarTower A B N Algebra.toSMul
        (@SMulZeroClass.toSMul B N _ (@SMulWithZero.toSMulZeroClass B N _ _
          (@MulActionWithZero.toSMulWithZero B N _ _
            (@Module.toMulActionWithZero B N _ _ iMB))))
        iA.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul) →
      @GenericallyFree A _ N iACG iA)
    ?_ ?_ ?_ ‹Module A M› ‹IsScalarTower A B M›
  · intro N _ _ _ _ iA _
    exact @genericallyFree_of_subsingleton A N _ _ _ iA ‹_›
  · intro N _ _ _ p e iA htower
    letI := iA
    haveI : IsScalarTower A B N := htower
    exact (genericallyFree_quotient_prime A B p.1).of_linearEquiv
      (e.restrictScalars A).symm
  · intro N₁ _ _ _ N₂ _ _ _ N₃ _ _ _ u v hu hv huv h₁ h₃ iA₂ htower₂
    letI iA₁ : Module A N₁ := Module.compHom N₁ (algebraMap A B)
    letI iA₃ : Module A N₃ := Module.compHom N₃ (algebraMap A B)
    haveI ht₁ : IsScalarTower A B N₁ :=
      ⟨fun a b n => by
        show (a • b) • n = algebraMap A B a • b • n
        rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]⟩
    haveI ht₃ : IsScalarTower A B N₃ :=
      ⟨fun a b n => by
        show (a • b) • n = algebraMap A B a • b • n
        rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]⟩
    letI := iA₂
    haveI : IsScalarTower A B N₂ := htower₂
    exact genericallyFree_of_exact (u.restrictScalars A) (v.restrictScalars A)
      hu hv huv (h₁ iA₁ ht₁) (h₃ iA₃ ht₃)

end GenericFreeness
